# Fibonacci layers generated by doubling and two reflections

**Mark Vladimir Prizmic · Research note · Version 0.1 · November 27, 2026**

[Paper (PDF)](paper.pdf) · [LaTeX source](paper.tex) · [Verification code](verify_distance.py) · [Retained results](verification.json)

## Theorem

Start with $G_1=\{1\}$. Apply $x\mapsto2x$, $x\mapsto1-x$, and $x\mapsto2-x$ to each layer, excluding every integer already encountered. Every integer appears in exactly one layer. With $F_0=0$ and $F_1=1$,

$$|G_n|=2F_{n-1},\qquad |G_n\cap\mathbb Z_{>0}|=F_{n-1}\quad(n\ge2).$$

For $n\ge4$, the even and odd counts are $2F_{n-2}$ and $2F_{n-3}$, respectively. The parity formulas require these initial exceptions: layers 1, 2, and 3 have even/odd counts $(0,1)$, $(2,0)$, and $(1,1)$. Layer 2 is $\{0,2\}$, so its nonpositive member is zero.

The paper proves an exact recursive shortest-path distance and derives the distance generating function

$$1+\frac{2z}{1-z-z^2}.$$

## Reproduce the finite checks

From this directory, using Python 3.10 or later with its standard library:

```bash
python3 verify_distance.py --max-distance 25 --edge-radius 100000 > verification.json
```

The retained run independently generates all **392,835 integers through distance 25**, compares their distances with the proved formula, and checks the counts and edge inequalities. The JSON report is a finite implementation check; the paper supplies the proof for all layers. Run Python normally, without `-O`, so its assertions remain enabled.

## Sources and research status

The original sequence and conjectures are due to **Clark Kimberling**, [OEIS A242364](https://oeis.org/A242364), June 11, 2014. The definition here follows the entry's program and examples by explicitly removing earlier layers. Related work by [Danielle Cox and Karyn McLellan](https://www.fq.math.ca/Papers1/55-2/CoxMcLellan021717.pdf), *The Fibonacci Quarterly* 55 (2017), 105–113, treats the two-map system without $x\mapsto2-x$.

The proof, manuscript, and code were developed with substantial assistance from **OpenAI's ChatGPT**, with additional AI-assisted mathematical reviews. This version has **not received external human peer review or proof-assistant certification**. The literature check is limited, and **no priority or first-proof claim is made**.
